title: POC Infosec Workshop & Evidence Packet
content:
Purpose:
This document captures the outcomes, answers, and evidence items produced during the December 12, 2024 POC infosec workshop with AcadiaTech (POC customer). It is intended for: (a) packaging an evidence packet for the customer's security team, (b) tracking outstanding evidence items for the solutions engineering (SE) and security teams, and (c) providing a concise mapping of Redwood controls to the customer's questionnaire asks.

Scope:
- Redwood hosted inference (Redwood API) used for POC.
- Dedicated test VPC (dev) provisioned in us-west-2 for customer testing.
- Data flow: customer sends text to Redwood API over TLS; inference occurs on dedicated pool; responses returned to customer endpoint.
- No customer data persisted to long-term storage during the POC (ephemeral KV cache only).

Attendees (workshop):
- Priya Raman (Redwood, Infosec Lead)
- Daniel K. Lee (Solutions Engineering)
- Sofia Martinez (Platform Eng)
- Evan Brooks (Customer Success)
- Alex Carter (AcadiaTech, Security)
- Maria Gomez (AcadiaTech, Platform)

Summary of customer asks and Redwood short answers (workshop-level):
1) Network isolation and egress control:
   - Ask: Can POC workloads be isolated in a customer-specific VPC with controlled egress?
   - Short answer: Yes. Dedicated test VPC in us-west-2 was provisioned. Egress is restricted via NAT gateway and customer-requested firewall rules.
   - Evidence: architecture-diagram.png (s3://redwood-evidence/pocs/acadiatech/architecture-diagram.png), vpc-config.json (Drive link below).

2) Data residency and retention:
   - Ask: Are tokens and request logs retained? Where? For how long?
   - Short answer: By default, request metadata and short-term debug logs retained for 7 days in the hosted telemetry system. No PII is stored. For POC we configured retention to 24 hours and retention policy is documented.
   - Evidence: telemetry-retention-policy.pdf, log-retention-config-20241210.json

3) Encryption (in transit & at rest) and key management:
   - Ask: TLS, encryption at rest, KMS/HSM usage, key rotation.
   - Short answer: All traffic uses TLS 1.2+/modern cipher suites. Customer data at rest on provisioned storage is encrypted with AWS KMS CMKs. KMS key policy excerpt and rotation schedule included. We can support customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private modes.
   - Evidence: kms-policy-snippet.txt, tls-cipher-scan.txt

4) Access control and authentication:
   - Ask: Role-based access, least privilege, audit logs for admin ops.
   - Short answer: We map Redwood console and infra roles to RBAC groups (eng, se, infra, srep). Admin operations require MFA and are logged to the centralized audit log. For this POC only invited engineers have access; their access review screenshot included.
   - Evidence: rbac-screenshot.png, admin-audit-log-extract-20241212.csv

5) Patch management and vulnerability scanning:
   - Ask: Image vulnerability scanning cadence and exception process.
   - Short answer: We run daily image scans using our CI pipeline (Clair/Trivy integration). Critical CVEs trigger automated rebuilds and work items.
   - Evidence: vuln-scan-report-20241211.pdf, ci-pipeline-job-5432 (GitHub Actions run link).

Control mapping (extracted for quick review):
- Encryption at rest -> SOC2 CC6, CC7
- Access controls & RBAC -> SOC2 CC2, CC3
- Logging & monitoring -> SOC2 CC7
- Change management & patching -> SOC2 CC5

- vpc-config.json (Drive: /shared_drives/security-and-compliance/poc-acadiatech/vpc-config.json)
- kms-policy-snippet.txt (Drive link)

- incident-response-runbook-excerpt.md (Drive link)

Open / outstanding items (action owner and ETA):
- Item A: Provide customer-managed KMS example policy and steps to enable CMK in Dedicated mode. Owner: Sofia Martinez. ETA: 2024-12-22.
- Item B: Exported end-to-end TLS configuration for load balancer + client handshake logs for their pen-test team. Owner: Daniel K. Lee. ETA: 2024-12-20.
- Item C: Formal SOC2 mapping document with statement for POC scope (incomplete). Owner: Priya Raman (security). ETA: 2025-01-05.

Workshop notes / working discussion highlights (verbatim snippets):
- "Customer wants proof they can disable all outbound connections except to our telemetry endpoint — we showed firewall rules and suggested a network ACL approach. Need to get ACL snippet into packet."
- "AcadiaTech prefers KMS CMKs managed by them for production — noted: we can enable in Dedicated, Private requires on-prem HSM integration planning."
- "Agreement: for POC we will not persist raw customer payload beyond ephemeral cache; will share cache purge logs."

Risk & mitigations observed during POC:
- Risk: Potential exposure through debug endpoints if left enabled. Mitigation: debug endpoints disabled by default in POC environment; audit confirms off.
- Risk: Temporary elevated access for SE during troubleshooting. Mitigation: access is time-limited (1 day) and logged; we included audit extraction showing time-limited grants.

Customer-facing recommended packet structure (what we will deliver):
1) Cover note + summary (this doc)
2) Architecture diagram + network config snippets
3) KMS & encryption docs + CMK enablement steps
4) RBAC & admin audit logs (redacted)
5) Vulnerability scan & patching summary
6) Retention & telemetry policy excerpts
7) Open items tracker and point of contact

Next steps (immediate):
- SE to assemble Drive folder and S3 evidence bundle and share signed link with AcadiaTech. (Owner: Daniel)
- Priya to produce SOC2 mapping paragraph specifically limited to POC footprint and redact any unrelated controls. (Owner: Priya)
- Sofia to deliver CMK policy example and enablement checklist. (Owner: Sofia)

Notes to internal reviewers (security):
- Redact any internal IPs before handing to customer.
- Replace developer usernames with role labels in audit extracts (e.g., se-engineer-1).
- Validate there are no sample payloads in logs that contain PII.

Appendix: quick-copy sample answers for questionnaire (deliverable snippets)
Q: How is data encrypted at rest?
A: All data at rest in the POC environment is encrypted using AES-256 via AWS KMS-managed CMKs. Keys are rotated per policy and we can support customer-managed CMKs for Dedicated and Private deployment modes. Evidence: kms-policy-snippet.txt and kms-rotation-schedule.pdf.

Q: Who has administrative access to the POC environment?
A: Administrative access is limited to the named Redwood SE and infra engineers for the duration of the POC, enforced via RBAC groups, MFA, and time-limited session tokens. Audit logs of admin actions are included for the POC period.

End of document.

(Drive folder to populate: /shared_drives/security-and-compliance/pocs/acadiatech/ -> will contain the listed artifacts and a signed link to S3 evidence bundle.)
